items.title: 14.2.3 Projection of a Vector along Another Vector (Roman Urdu)

blocks.text: Ab dot product ka sab se khoobsurat geometrical matlab samajhte hain. Kai physical maamlon mein yeh jaanna zaroori hota hai ke kisi vector ka "kitna hissa" kisi khaas simt (direction) mein lag raha hai. Misaal ke taur par, aap suitcase ko uske handle se tircha kheench rahe hain; aap ki taaqat ka kitna hissa suitcase ko aage barha raha hai? Aise sawalon ke liye hum ek vector ki doosre vector ke saath projection (saya) nikalte hain.
Farz karein \(\overrightarrow{OA} = \underline{u}\) aur \(\overrightarrow{OB} = \underline{v}\), aur in ke darmiyan angle \(\theta\) hai, jahan \(0 \le \theta \le \pi\).

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab mein "Let 0 be the angle between them, such that 0 ≤ 0 ≤ π" chhapa hai: harf θ ki jagah hindsa 0 chhap gaya hai. Sahi jumla: \(\theta\) un ke darmiyan angle hai, aur \(0 \le \theta \le \pi\).

Ab \(B\) se \(OA\) par ek perpendicular \(\overline{BM}\) giraiye (\(\overline{BM} \perp \overline{OA}\)). To \(\overline{OM}\) ko \(\underline{u}\) ke saath \(\underline{v}\) ki projection kehte hain.

blocks.alt: Vector u along the horizontal line from O to A and vector v from O to B making angle theta with OA. A dashed perpendicular drops from B to the point M on OA, with a right-angle mark at M. Below, the length OM is marked as the magnitude of v times cos theta.
blocks.caption: Figure: OM = |v| cos θ is the projection of v along u (original drawing after the textbook's figure)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Projection ko saaye (shadow) ki tarah sochiye. Farz karein roshni \(\underline{u}\) wali line par bilkul seedhi (perpendicular) gir rahi hai. To \(\underline{v}\) ka jo saya \(\underline{u}\) ki line par banega, woh \(\overline{OM}\) hai. Dopahar ke waqt khambay ka saya zameen par isi tarah banta hai.

Figure se, right triangle \(OMB\) mein:
\[\dfrac{\overline{OM}}{\overline{OB}} = \cos\theta\]
yani
\[\overline{OM} = |\overline{OB}|\cos\theta\]
\[= |\underline{v}|\cos\theta \quad \text{...(1)}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kyun: right triangle \(OMB\) mein \(\overline{OB} = |\underline{v}|\) hypotenuse (sab se lambi side, right angle ke saamne) hai, aur \(\overline{OM}\) angle \(\theta\) ke saath wali side (adjacent) hai. Trigonometry se: adjacent = hypotenuse \(\times \cos\theta\). Bas yahi (1) hai.

Ab dot product ki definition mein yeh rakhte hain:
\[\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\cos\theta\]
\[= |\underline{u}|(|\underline{v}|\cos\theta)\]
\[= |\underline{u}|(\overline{OM})\]
= (\(\underline{u}\) ki magnitude) (\(\underline{u}\) ke saath \(\underline{v}\) ki projection)

Is tarah geometrically (shakal ke lehaaz se) do vectors ka dot product ek vector ki magnitude aur doosre vector ki us par projection ka product hai. Doosre lafzon mein, dot product batata hai ke ek vector doosre ki simt mein kitna phaila hua hai.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Agar \(\underline{v}\) bilkul \(\underline{u}\) ke perpendicular ho, to us ka saya kitna lamba hoga? Socheiye: roshni seedhi oopar se gir rahi hai aur khamba bhi seedha khara hai... saya sirf ek point hai, yani lambai \(0\). Is liye projection \(0\), aur dot product bhi \(0\). Aur agar angle obtuse ho to \(M\) point \(O\) ke doosri taraf girta hai, is liye projection negative aati hai.

Ab projection ko components se nikalne wala formula banate hain. Definition se:
\[\cos\theta = \dfrac{\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}}{|\underline{u}||\underline{v}|} \quad \text{...(2)}\]
(1) aur (2) ko mila kar:
\[\overline{OM} = |\underline{v}| \cdot \dfrac{\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}}{|\underline{u}||\underline{v}|}\]
\[= \dfrac{\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}}{|\underline{u}|}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Kyun: (1) mein \(\cos\theta\) tha jo humein aksar maloom nahin hota. (2) se \(\cos\theta\) ki jagah \(\frac{\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}}{|\underline{u}||\underline{v}|}\) rakh diya, jo components se aasani se nikal aata hai. \(|\underline{v}|\) upar neeche cancel ho gaya, aur bahut saaf formula bacha.

blocks.text_alt: projection of v along u equals u dot v over the magnitude of u
projection of u along v equals u dot v over the magnitude of v

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Yaad rakhne ka tareeqa: "jis vector ke saath (along) projection leni hai, usi ki lambai se divide karo". \(\underline{v}\) along \(\underline{u}\): \(|\underline{u}|\) se divide. \(\underline{u}\) along \(\underline{v}\): \(|\underline{v}|\) se divide. Upar dot product dono mein ek hi hai.
Dhyan dein: projection ek scalar (number) hai, jo positive, negative ya zero ho sakta hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Hamari practice, kitab ka sawal nahin.) \(\underline{u} = 2\underline{i} - \underline{j} + 2\underline{k}\), \(\underline{v} = \underline{i} + \underline{j} + \underline{k}\).
Pehle dot product aur lambaiyan:
\[\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 2 - 1 + 2 = 3\]
\[|\underline{u}| = \sqrt{4 + 1 + 4} = 3,\quad |\underline{v}| = \sqrt{3}\]
Ab dono projections:
\[\text{proj. of } \underline{v} \text{ along } \underline{u} = \tfrac{3}{3} = 1\]
\[\text{proj. of } \underline{u} \text{ along } \underline{v} = \tfrac{3}{\sqrt{3}} = \sqrt{3}\]
Dekhiye, dono jawab alag hain! Is liye sawal ko ghor se parhiye ke kis ki projection kis ke saath maangi gayi hai.
Tasdeeq: \(|\underline{u}| \times (\text{proj. of } \underline{v} \text{ along } \underline{u}) = 3 \times 1 = 3 = \underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}\). Sahi!

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Shuru wali suitcase ki misaal ab hal karte hain. Farz karein aap handle ko \(50\) newton ki force se kheench rahe hain aur handle zameen se \(60^{\circ}\) ka angle bana raha hai. Suitcase zameen ke saath saath chalta hai, yani harkat ki simt horizontal hai. To force ka kaam aane wala hissa harkat ki simt mein force ki projection hai: \(50\cos 60^{\circ} = 50 \times \frac{1}{2} = 25\) newton. Yani aadhi taaqat aage kheench rahi hai aur baqi aadhi suitcase ko upar uthane ki koshish mein lag rahi hai. Is liye bhaari cheez ko jitna seedha (zameen ke qareeb) kheenchein, utni aasani hoti hai. Yahi soch 14.2.8 mein work ke formula ki bunyaad banegi.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(\underline{u}\) ke saath \(\underline{v}\) ki projection \(= |\underline{v}|\cos\theta = \frac{\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}}{|\underline{u}|}\).
2. \(\underline{v}\) ke saath \(\underline{u}\) ki projection \(= |\underline{u}|\cos\theta = \frac{\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}}{|\underline{v}|}\).
3. Geometry: \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = |\underline{u}| \times\) (\(\underline{u}\) par \(\underline{v}\) ka saya).
4. Projection number hai; obtuse angle par negative, perpendicular par zero.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Ghalat lambai se divide karna: "\(\underline{v}\) along \(\underline{u}\)" mein \(|\underline{u}|\) se divide hota hai, \(|\underline{v}|\) se nahin.
2. Jawab ko vector bana dena, jaise \(\frac{\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}}{|\underline{u}|^{2}}\underline{u}\). Woh "vector projection" hai jo is kitab mein define nahin; kitab ki projection sirf number \(\frac{\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}}{|\underline{u}|}\) hai.
3. Negative projection ko ghalat samajh kar sign hata dena. Obtuse angle par negative jawab bilkul sahi hai.
